tb21_profile.skill: Complete a machine-checked inductive proof: pick the right induction, supply the missing helper lemmas (n+0=n, n+S m=S(n+m)), drive a tactic language, and iterate until the kernel accepts it
tb21_profile.domain: Coq / dependently typed proof assistants, Peano arithmetic on nat, coqc toolchain and formal verification
tb21_profile.task_form: complete-a-partial-artifact until a strict checker accepts it; success is binary and decided by the tool, not by tests

searches: tools.py search all "prove that|formal (proof|verification)|induction hypothesis|lemma|SMT solver|Z3|symbolic execution" -n 30
tools.py search all "Haskell|ghc |type checker|typecheck|mypy|sympy|SAT solver|model check|Alloy|Idris|Prolog" -n 30
tools.py search all "z3|constraint solver|satisfiab|first-order logic|inference rules|rewrite rules|term rewriting" -n 25
tools.py search all "Peano|natural number|recursive definition|proof tree|LaTeX proof|sequent" -n 25
tools.py search tmax "borrow checker|lifetime (issue|error)|type error|does not typecheck" -n 15

Peano Nat with recursive plus and mult in Haskell: the exact inductive structure the theorem quantifies over
Assembles a formal derivation tree from proof steps and typesets it; keeps the shape of a proof in view

notes: The pool contains zero Coq tasks, but eight near-duplicates of this exact theorem in Agda (seven in Recursive-Task-Synthesis, one in TerminalWorld), all requiring the same two helper lemmas and a checker-accepted, goal-free result; those honestly occupy eight of the final ten. TMax has nothing formal: its best offerings are constraint-solver tasks (logical decision procedures) and Rust borrow-checker fixes (edit-until-the-static-checker-accepts), and I scored them 2-3 accordingly rather than inflating them. For SWE-Smith and SWE-Rebench I ignored the lexically retrieved 'proof-of-work' and 'proof-of-concept exploit' hits entirely (pure keyword collision with 'proof') and went for type inference, symbolic algebra and semantics-preserving rewriting instead.
